verdict.rationale: The Drive API's own authorization model supports least-privilege OAuth scopes, defined in both the Cloud console and the app. One narrow scope limits access to only the specific files used with the app, so a credential granted to an agent can be scoped down. However, the evidence documents scope definition rather than issuing distinct credentials for an agent, and nothing shows agent-specific credential management. missing for 10: documented flow for issuing per-agent credentials (e.g. service accounts or tokens), revocation and rotation controls, a full scope catalog, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: To authorize your app, the Google Drive API requires you to define OAuth scopes in two places: the Google Cloud console and your app.
See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app
